item.text:
**Verdict:** Mostly no. The 2023 record shows widespread abuse by police, prison staff, intelligence services, and Kremlin-linked proxy forces, with only isolated, local accountability cases and no sign of a systematic protection or punishment campaign.

| Claim | Source | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Widespread abuse and impunity | U.S. Department of State, *2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia* | 22 Apr 2024 | https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia | The report says authorities jailed antiwar protesters and opposition figures, used torture and harsh prison conditions, and did not take adequate steps to punish most officials; it also says Kremlin-backed Wagner committed widespread abuses and authorities did not investigate or prosecute them. | 3B.2, 3B.1, 2B.9 |
| Rare accountability case inside a broader impunity pattern | U.S. Department of State, *2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia* | 22 Apr 2024 | https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia | The same report notes one of the few accountability examples: five police officers in Tatarstan were convicted for torturing a prisoner who later died. The report frames this as exceptional, not systemic. | 3B.2 |
| State forces committed severe abuses | U.S. Department of State, press briefing on crimes against humanity designation | 22 Feb 2023 | https://2021-2025.state.gov/press-briefing-on-crimes-against-human-rights-designation-by-dr-beth-van-schaack-ambassador-at-large-for-global-criminal-justice/ | The State Department said members of Russia’s forces and other officials committed crimes against humanity, including execution-style killings, torture, rape, and deportation of civilians and children. That is strong evidence of tolerated or unrestrained abuse by state actors. | 3B.2, 3B.1, 2B.9 |
| Police and prison abuse continued | Human Rights Watch, *World Report 2024: Russia* | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/russia | HRW says police beat anti-war protesters, authorities tortured detainees in custody, and prison administrators repeatedly used punitive disciplinary cells against Navalny and other political prisoners, with no meaningful investigation. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Excessive force and torture after arrest | Freedom House, *Freedom in the World 2023: Russia* | 2023 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023 | Freedom House reports security personnel used excessive force to disperse anti-war protests, detainees were mistreated and tortured in custody, and authorities criminalized peaceful dissent rather than restraining abuse. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |

Search gap: I found no credible 2023 evidence that Putin launched a broad, sustained effort to prevent abuse by police, intelligence services, prisons, or proxy forces. The only counterexample I found was an isolated local conviction in Tatarstan, which does not rebut the wider pattern of tolerance and impunity.
